tasks.gr8-reading-a-poem-t1: Topic: Reading a poem. Cover the key features of a poem (lines, stanzas, speaker, title, typography and layout), literal and figurative meaning, and how to read a poem aloud with attention to punctuation and line ends. Use only original poems or public-domain poems that are cited. Ask Grade 8 learners to say what a poem is saying and how it says it, quoting the lines that show it.
tasks.gr8-figures-of-speech-in-poems-t2: Topic: Figures of speech in poems. Cover simile, metaphor, personification, hyperbole and onomatopoeia, how to recognise each, and how to explain the effect of a figure of speech in a poem. Use only original poems or public-domain poems that are cited. Ask Grade 8 learners to name the figure, say what is compared, and explain the effect.
tasks.gr8-sound-and-structure-in-poems-t3: Topic: Sound and structure in poems. Cover rhyme and rhyme scheme (labelled with letters), rhythm and beat, alliteration, repetition and the refrain, and how sound and structure add to meaning. Use only original poems or public-domain poems that are cited. Ask Grade 8 learners to mark rhyme schemes, to find sound devices and to explain what they add.
tasks.gr8-mood-tone-theme-and-poetry-questions: Topic: Mood, tone, theme and contextual poetry questions. Cover mood (the feeling the poem creates in the reader), tone (the attitude of the speaker or poet), theme (the main idea), how to answer contextual poetry questions (read the question, quote and explain, check marks) and how to write a short poem of three to four verses. Use only original poems. Ask Grade 8 learners to support every answer with words from the poem.
